frames.review_note: Minor, retouch if possible: the two palanquins seen through the gate stand on small wheels under their carrying poles (about x 0.22-0.30, y 0.75-0.82). Palanquins are carried, and in 1.2 and 1.5 they rest on legs. The guards carry spears as well as their swords and round shields. Otherwise clean: dusk estate, gatehouse, Nair guards watching the road, a servant lighting wall-niche lamps, road dust and the jackfruit tree. No text. The wide quiet dusk sky across the top has room for the long caption.

Varma's hair knot sits at the back of his crown, not the bible's side knot above the LEFT ear. Otherwise he follows the private-visit look: bare-headed, no turban, crest or spear, the V13 face and moustache, gold necklaces, a cream and gold mundu. He also has a gold-bordered shoulder cloth. The Rani matches her sheet: severe bun with no flowers, white sari with a narrow gold border, gold ear studs. The Prince, about ten, wears a white mundu, a thin gold chain and a small topknot. Ornate and plainer palanquins rest on legs, which is right. The sky above the gate at the upper left has room for the caption.

Minor background details: three palanquins appear beyond the gate opening rather than two just inside it, and Padmini shows little grey threading. Otherwise clean. Padmini matches her sheet and stands on the verandah above the steps: old Kerala drape with no blouse, a white and gold sari, jasmine in her hair, a gold chain, walking stick in hand. She has a set face and looks off-panel left across the courtyard. The open dusk sky between the jackfruit tree and the roof has room for both balloons.

Minor background-only issues: the two palanquins beyond the gateway look like they sit on small wheels rather than being set down on their poles, and the gate guards hold spears with their round shields rather than swords. Both are small, far back, and do not affect the beat. Nagoji matches the sheet and the ch17 bible row: rust-red turban, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small flush gold ear stud, long curly black hair, cream tunic with broad red sash, cream trousers, barefoot, no talwar. He is caught half-turned under the jackfruit tree in deep shade, glancing back over his shoulder, with one bare foot on the side path. Hands and feet are sound and there is no painted text. Clear dusk sky over the gatehouse (upper middle, about x 0.55 to 0.95, y 0.03 to 0.18) leaves room for his balloon without covering his face.

Continuity with 1.3 is weak. Padmini stands at courtyard level beside the foot of the verandah plinth instead of up on the verandah. She looks right toward the house, where in 1.3 she looks left across the courtyard toward the tree where Nagoji is, and her pose has a slight forward lean. Otherwise this is the closest likeness to her sheet on the page: deep-lined stern face, gold bead chain, ball ear studs, jasmine at a nape coil with grey threading, old drape with no blouse, stick in hand. Lit lamp niches are behind her, the palanquins rest on legs inside the gate, and there is no text. The dusk sky at the upper left and centre has room for the balloon.

Minor only. The King kneels at the foot of the steps, not on them, and his hands are on Padmini's feet. His hair has a few grey-looking highlight strands, and the knot sits toward the back of the head. Padmini's grey is a little heavier than a light threading. The gate guards carry spears and shields where the script asks for swords. Nagoji matches the sheet: turban, tunic, red sash, barefoot, moustache, clean chin and gold stud. Lettering: put the Varma balloon in the sky gap between the jackfruit foliage and the roof (upper middle), and the caption on the clear courtyard floor at bottom left or along the top-left edge.

Acceptable with minor issues. The close-up of the Prince matches his sheet: white forehead mark, thin gold chain, bare-chested, topknot, watchful frown. Two small problems. His curls are looser than the sheet's neat topknot, and the ear studs he wears in 2.2 and 2.4 are missing here. He also looks screen-left here but screen-right toward Nagoji in 2.4, a mild flip in screen direction. Nagoji is correctly off-panel to the upper left. Wide clear sunset sky across the upper left takes both balloons.

Acceptable. This is a low-angle two-shot with the boy looking up and Nagoji looking down. Nagoji has the rust-red turban, cream tunic with sleeves down (brand hidden), broad red sash, cream trousers and long curly black hair. He has the thick curled moustache, a clean-shaven chin and a tiny flush gold stud, and his feet are out of frame. His expression is a touch stern rather than gently serious. Hands are sound. The Prince's forehead mark from the sheet does not show at this angle. Open dusk sky between the tree and Nagoji's head, plus the leaves at upper left, gives room for three balloons.

Minor only. The King is smiling openly rather than hiding his amusement. The Rani and the King wear a white forehead namam that is not on their sheets, though it matches the Prince's. The gate guards are in back view. The ornament along the palanquin valance is decorative, not lettering. The Rani's hand is reaching his shoulder and her fingers are sound. Lettering: put the two Prince balloons in the sky gap above and right of his head, between the tree and the roof, or in the upper left above the gatehouse roof.

Minor only. The Rani's hair has a faint grey sheen not on her sheet. Clear sky above the centre is limited, so the two Rani balloons may need to sit over the upper-left foliage and gate roof, with the caption on the open earth at lower left. Faces and the hand on the shoulder stay clear. Otherwise clean: hand on the Prince's shoulder, both looking off right toward Nagoji, the Prince matches his sheet (forehead mark, topknot, chain), and the courtyard, gate, guards and dusk match 2.5.

Clean. Nagoji inclines his head with his hands clasped, and the Rani is already turning away toward the verandah steps and the house. Nagoji is in the commander look, barefoot, with a clean-shaven chin under a curled moustache and a small gold stud. The white scar shows on his LEFT forearm, the correct side, and the brand is not legible. The Rani matches her sheet (no flowers, no mark). The courtyard and dusk light continue from 3.1. Open sky at upper centre takes both balloons.

v03 is the best of the three and can be used. It fixes the main faults in v02: Padmini now wears the old blouseless Kerala drape, and the red-and-white namam on Nagoji's forehead is gone. Nagoji matches his sheet: thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold stud, long curly black hair, rust turban, cream tunic with broad red sash, cream trousers, barefoot, standing apart at the right edge of the light. The Rani has no jasmine and stands upright in white with a gold border. Padmini has jasmine and her stick beside her. Varma is bare-headed in a cream mundu with gold necklaces and no spear. Ramayyan is thin, with receding hair, white cloth, a palm-leaf bundle and a stylus. The storeroom doorway with clay vessels is visible. There is no painted text, balloon, gore or anachronism. Captions fit in the evening sky and over the low-detail roof tiles across the top left and centre (about x 0.12 to 0.65, y 0.0 to 0.2), clear of every face. Remaining faults for the author: (1) a faint pale streak above Nagoji's left eyebrow at the turban edge. It is probably a highlight, but it could read as a trace of the removed forehead mark. (2) The Prince has a white-and-red namam and gold ear studs. His hair is a bun at the back of the head, not a small neat topknot. He sits with arms folded on his knees, so he does not copy Varma's hands-on-knees posture exactly. (3) Varma's side knot sits at the crown on the far side of the head, so it reads more like a top knot than one above the left ear. (4) The view is close to eye level from the edge of the sunken court, not the script's high corner, so the square of open sky is smaller than described. (5) Ramayyan is well lit, not half in shadow. (6) A few burlap-like sacks sit among the clay vessels in the storeroom doorway. (7) Padmini's hair reads as noticeably grey-streaked, not thick black with a light threading of grey.

Minor: the low door in the storeroom's far corner is a little more visible than 'barely visible' and has a ring handle. A few woven sacks sit on the storeroom floor. The King stands with the same upper cloth as in 4.2. The King's right arm and pointing hand are sound and point across the court into the open doorway, where clay rice vessels taller than a man's waist are visible. The face and moustache match the sheet, with a pearl earring, bare-headed and bare-chested. The sky and roof at top centre-right take the balloon.

Clean. Muted lamp-brown flashback palette with soft irregular edges. Young Varma, gaunt and wide-eyed, with matted hair and a torn dark-brown waist-cloth, no gold, crouches knees-up between clay grain jars. The scene has straw-bound paddy bundles, a woven mat, cobwebs, low beams and slits of light through the plank floor above, with no burlap sacks and no lamp. The low-detail earth wall and ceiling area above and right of the boy takes the off-panel balloon. The tail runs to the top edge, toward the present-day King above.

Minor: the bowl of rice reads as untouched with a few stray grains on the mat, but the 'pushed away' gesture is only implied by its placement at the mat's edge. Everything else is clean. It has three separate torn-edge slivers in the muted lamp-brown memory palette. The guard's hands drop gold fanams onto his palm, the anatomy is sound, the coins carry no markings and his sword hilt is at his waist. A barefoot figure in a mundu and red sash holds a drawn blade on a moonlit laterite-walled road, seen from behind with no face showing. There is no text, blood or anachronism, and a wide plain parchment band across the top holds both off-panel Varma balloons.

Minor: the palette is warm full colour rather than the muted lamp-brown memory palette of 5.1. Young Padmini's white sari has a gold border instead of being plain. Every beat is present: the storeroom, the clay vessels, the post, one torch held by a retainer, retainers with swords and round shields, and an older grey-haired leader with gold earrings and his sword drawn. A knife is held against the throat of the bare-chested husband pinned at the post, with no blood. Young Padmini, unlined, with black hair coiled with jasmine, stands empty-handed facing the leader, and the swaddled infant sleeps in a cloth cradle seen through the doorway. There is no cup and no text, and the hands are sound. Space for the off-panel balloon is on the dark wall above the doorway (x 0.3-0.55, y 0-0.1).

Minor only. The Prince's curly hair is fuller than a 'small neat topknot', though it is gathered into a knot on top. Varma matches his sheet closely: black side knot behind the left ear, pearl ear drop, curled moustache, beaded gold necklaces, cream mundu with a gold border, bare-chested and bare-headed. The setting (nalukettu courtyard, carved elephant pillars, open-wick brass lamps, black mirror floor, evening sky) matches panels 5.4 and 5.5. There is no painted text, and the stools and hands are sound. Varma's short balloon can sit in the open sky and roof area at the top centre (x 0.25 to 0.55, y 0 to 0.15), clear of both faces.

None significant. Ramayyan matches his sheet: thin, sharp features, receding hair with curly sides, plain unbordered white cloth, no forehead mark or sacred thread. His arms are folded over the palm-leaf bundle, with the stylus in hand. He is lit fairly evenly rather than standing at the edge of the lamplight. The upper right sky and roof leave ample room for the balloon.

Minor. Both men stand, while the King is seated in 6.4 and 7.1. Varma adds gold armlets, a gold belt and a gold-bordered shoulder cloth not seen in 6.2 and 6.4, though the shoulder cloth also appears in 5.5 and 7.2. His hairline is high, but his face, moustache, pearl ear drop and black hair knot match his sheet. Ramayyan holds out a single rolled leaf tied with saffron thread, with no script on it. The King's hands stay at his sides and his sideways look is dry. Hands are sound. The sky, roof and lattice between the two heads leave room for both balloons.

Minor only. Two tiny out-of-focus wall lanterns in the background (left of centre behind Nagoji's hair and at the far left edge) read as small enclosed lantern housings rather than open-wick lamps; they are negligible at page size. Padmini's grey threading is not visible, and her face is cropped by the right edge, which suits the 'at the panel's edge' direction. Otherwise clean: Nagoji has the curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small flush gold stud, rust-red turban, cream tunic and red sash, and is lamplit and still. Padmini has jasmine, the gold chain, no blouse, and her stick, and she leans forward from a wooden stool as if rising. The setting is the nalukettu courtyard with carved elephant pillars, rice vessels and the black floor. There is no painted text and hands are sound. The caption fits top-left over the roof and sky, above the turban.

Minor only. Padmini's hands look somewhat older than her fifties. Her upper hand's fingers wrap under his wrist in a slightly tangled way but still read. Otherwise the beat is clean. It is a tight insert of his LEFT hand turned palm up, with the cream sleeve pushed back and the red sash at the edge. The brand is a pale, raised, ridged patch on the inner wrist with no legible letters, and the long white scar runs up the forearm. Her thumb rests on the brand and her work-rough hands wear gold bangles. Her face is cropped above the frame, so the tails go to the top edge. The upper-left sleeve and upper-centre background (x 0.0-0.65, y 0.0-0.3) take both balloons.

Minor only: close-up so Padmini's walking stick is out of frame; Nagoji is seen from behind (turban, gold stud, curly hair consistent). Grip on his LEFT wrist with brand and white scar on the inner forearm, Padmini's wet eyes, jasmine, black hair with grey, gold chain, Kerala drape with no blouse all correct. Lettering space over the roof and sky at top centre and the lattice at top left.

Minor: a small maroon patch shows at Padmini's chest under the sari edge (reads as shadowed inner cloth, no sleeves); her walking stick is not shown. Otherwise strong: wide strip, Nagoji leaning back as if pulling away, she kisses the scarred inner left wrist, black mirror floor reflects both, turban on (correct before 8.4), clean chin and ear stud, storeroom jars and carved pillars match the setting. No text needed.

Minor issues only. Her hair shows rather more grey streaking than a light threading. Unlike the kneeling 8.2, she is now standing with her stick, which reads as her having risen. The beat is clear: eyes wet with a visible tear, face set like iron, head turning to her left toward the King off-panel. She matches her sheet, with jasmine, gold chain, Kerala drape and stick, in the same lamplit nalukettu. The dusk sky, roof and lattice at upper right and upper centre leave room for both balloons.

Minor: Padmini has a thin white sandal-paste line on her forehead that is not on her sheet or in 8.1/8.2 (small, not an identity break). Nagoji sits on a low wooden stool, bare-headed with loose curly hair, the folded rust turban in his hands and the sash still at his waist, no mark on his forehead (the Rani's fingertip only touches it). Rani with no jasmine, severe bun, white sari, gold ear studs, silver plate with brass lamp; Prince bare-chested with topknot, gold chain and white mundu, face tilted up; Padmini with jasmine and stick at his shoulder. Clear roof area at upper centre for the Rani's two short balloons.

Minor only. Varma's hair knot sits at the crown/back rather than clearly above the left ear, and he wears a white-and-red forehead namam that 9.1 does not show. The beat is correct: the Prince comes out of the storeroom first with wide eyes and dusty knees, and the King follows with a hand on the boy's shoulder, holding out the red-cloth bundle. Lamps are brass with open flames. The sky and roof at upper right are clear for the balloon.

Minor: a small near-black, faintly navy sleeve edge shows in the extreme lower-left corner where his cream tunic sleeve should be; at inset size it reads as shadow. Otherwise clean: tight inset of his right hand closing round the ivory grip with gold beaded guard and pommel matching 9.5's knife design, a plain unlettered conch outline struck into the steel near the hilt, left hand on the red cloth with the brand and scar on the inner left forearm, no painted text. Nagoji is the POV owner behind the camera (tail to bottom edge); Varma is off panel in front of him (tail to top edge); dark lamplit background upper centre-right holds both balloons.

Minor only. The brand on his raised LEFT forearm is a small, crisp reddish spiral near the elbow, not a pale ridged patch a hand's width above the wrist. At wide-shot scale it does not read as lettering. The knife grip reads brass/dark rather than the ivory of 9.5, which is negligible at this size. Otherwise it matches the beat: alone by the elephant pillar, arms raised gathering his hair into a knot, rust-red turban folded at his feet, tunic and red sash, barefoot, moustache, clean chin and gold stud, black floor holding the lamp reflections. The cream dhoti matches the page 9 frames. The night sky and roof at upper right are clear for both captions.

Minor only. This is a true close-up. The dark teak pillar with elephants climbing trunk to tail fills the image left, and his LEFT hand enters from the right with its fingertips on a carved elephant. The hand is sound: four fingers show and the thumb is hidden. On the inner left forearm are a pale, irregular, blurred scar patch above the wrist and one long thin white scar, as the r1 correction asked, with no symbol or tattoo. The rolled cream sleeve, low brass lamps, black reflective floor and courtyard match 10.1 and 10.4. Two small issues: a sliver of his face (nose, moustache and edge of the chin, with faint stubble grain) is cut off awkwardly in the top-right corner, and the rendering is a little more painterly and realistic than the inked line of 10.3. Neither matters much at panel scale. The upper band of dark sky and roof, from about x 0.4 to 0.9 and y 0 to 0.2, is clear for the long caption. Keep the caption left of the face sliver in the corner.

Acceptable with a framing note. The script asks for a tight insert at hip height. This is a medium back three-quarter view that includes his head in lost profile, so it is wider than scripted. The beat still reads clearly: the straight ivory knife grip with gold fittings, in a dark wooden sheath, sits in the red sash at his LEFT hip, and the fingertips of his LEFT hand rest on a carved elephant of the pillar. The r1 faults are all fixed. The arm is the left one, the brand is a pale blurred patch with one long thin white scar (no symbol and no X), and there is no bird-head grip. Identity matches the sheet and the bible row: thick curled moustache, flush gold ear stud, curly hair gathered in a knot on the crown, cream tunic, red sash and cream dhoti as in 10.1 and 10.4. There is a faint stipple of shadow on the jaw and chin, but no beard. The setting, the lamps burned low and the black reflective floor match the neighbouring panels. Both captions fit: the dark sky with palm silhouettes at upper right (x 0.75 to 1.0, y 0 to 0.12) and the dark roof eaves at upper centre-left (x 0.25 to 0.47, y 0 to 0.1). Keep both clear of the hair knot near x 0.6, y 0.03.

Minor. The framing is waist-up, not a tight face shot, but the beat reads: his face lit by low lamplight, turned up toward the elephants climbing the pillar into the roof dark, hair gathered at the crown. The brand is a dark blotchy mark rather than pale ridges, but it is blurred past reading and correctly placed on the inner LEFT forearm with the white scar. The knife hilt reads brass rather than ivory. Moustache, clean chin, gold stud and the first grey at the temple are all correct. Sky and dark roof at top centre are clear for the short caption.

Minor: Revathi has a tiny dark dot between the brows. It matches her approved sheet and is not a bright red bindi, so I accepted it. Everything else is clean. Nagoji: topknot with grey at the temple, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, flush gold stud, cream mundu with shoulder cloth, ivory conch knife at the waist fold, barefoot. Revathi arrives under the eaves with a damp sheen. The rain sheets off the tiled eaves and the jackfruit tree is in the courtyard. There is no painted text. Lettering space: the caption and Revathi's balloon fit over the roof beams at top centre, and Nagoji's balloon fits over the rain at top right.

Minor: a small red, glyph-like brand mark sits on Nagoji's outer upper LEFT arm. The bible puts the brand on the inner left forearm, though the long white scar on the left forearm is correct. The mark is small at panel scale, and a retouch to remove it would help. Revathi's faint orange parting line and small dark dot match her sheet. Otherwise clean: both sit side by side at the verandah edge, shoulders almost touching, with the rain curtain and jackfruit tree at left. He has the knot on the crown, first grey at the temple, moustache, clean chin and gold stud, the knife is at the mundu fold, and the rain and eaves at the top leave room for her two balloons.

Staging continuity: the two have swapped seats. In 11.1 and 11.3 Revathi is on the house side (left) and Nagoji on the rain side (right). Here Nagoji is on the left and Revathi on the right, with the same house-left and rain-right background. This is a soft 180-degree flip, not a hard failure, and it does give the right reading order (Nagoji speaks first). Everything else is clean. Nagoji has turned to look at her with the moustache, clean chin, gold stud, topknot and grey temple. Raindrops sit on Revathi's skin like pearls. The brand on his inner left forearm is an illegible puckered patch. No painted text. Lettering space: Revathi's balloon fits over the rain at top right and Nagoji's over the pillars and beams at top left or top centre.

Minor: Revathi stands rather than staying seated. This matches the v01 framing of 12.1, where they stand facing each other with his hand still held out. A faint red Y-shaped mark and a thin white scar line appear on Nagoji's right upper arm instead of his inner left forearm. They are faint enough to read as a scratch, but a retouch would help. Otherwise clean: Nagoji stands holding out his open left hand (sound anatomy) and Revathi looks down at it with her hands folded, not yet taking it. He has the knot on the crown, first grey at the temple, moustache, clean chin, gold stud, cream mundu and shoulder cloth, and the knife at the waist fold. Same verandah, rain and lamps, with rain and eaves at the top left for his balloon.

Minor issue only: the brand and white scar on Nagoji's inner left forearm are not visible on his outstretched left arm. Otherwise the panel is clean and matches the Ananthan Pillai sheet and the ch17 @11 bible row. Nagoji has a Kerala topknot with first grey at the temples, a thick curled moustache, a clean-shaven chin and a small flush gold stud. He wears a plain cream mundu with no border and a cream shoulder cloth, with the ivory conch-handled knife at the waist fold and no chain. Revathi matches her sheet: indigo sari with gold, jasmine braid, flat-coin necklace, armlets, sandalwood line, and no red dot or sindoor. The script beat reads clearly: his hand is still held out while her eyes go past him to the carved pillars and doorways. The setting is right, with rain sheeting off the eaves, the jackfruit tree and a wet verandah. There is no painted text and the hands are sound. Lettering space: the upper left rain and sky above his head and the rain between his head and the pillar can take the two Nagoji balloons. The eave roof at top centre or the dark lintel at upper right can take Revathi's balloon. Continuity note: the 11.5 and 12.2 v01 neighbours draw Nagoji with loose hair. This pick follows the bible's topknot, so the neighbours are the ones off-bible.

Minor only. A small brass lamp is already burning beside the cellar door, although the storeroom should be lit only by grey rain-light. The cellar door is ajar on its steps and is a little taller than a repair panel, but it is still low and in the far corner, matching the page 4 storeroom. Nagoji's temple grey is a broad streak, and there is light stubble shading on his jaw. The brand on his inner left forearm is a blurred, glyph-like burn, not readable. The beat works: he leads her by the hand between clay rice vessels taller than a man's waist, with rain-light from the doorway behind them. The plain dark plaster wall at the upper right has ample room for the caption.

Minor. The couple are drawn larger and better lit than the script's 'small and half-lost in the dark', so the clothed kiss shows directly as well as in the merged wall shadow. The lamp sits between the couple and the shadow, so physically the shadow falls the wrong way, which is a common comics cheat. Otherwise clean: Nagoji has the topknot, first grey, curled moustache, clean chin, small gold stud, shoulder cloth and mundu, conch knife and bare feet. Revathi has the indigo sari, jasmine braid, armlets and sandalwood line. The merged shadows on the earth wall carry the beat. There is room for two captions on the upper wall and beams and the lower-right wall.

Minor: a woven raised mat surface behind them reads a little like a backrest, though it is not a pillow. Her head rests on his shoulder and upper chest rather than mid-chest. Otherwise clean. Nagoji has a topknot, grey at the temples, a thick curled moustache, a clean chin and a flush gold stud. The raised LEFT forearm shows the ridged brand and the long white scar, with no letters. Revathi wears indigo with gold armlets, coin necklace, jasmine and the sandalwood line, with no red dot. Her fingertip is on the forearm right beside the brand. Lettering can sit over the large jars, paddy bundles at top left, or the white cloth at the bottom.

Continuity: the couple swap sides from 13.2. There Revathi lies on his right (image left); here she is on his left (image right), while the stairs, door and lamp stay on the right in both, so the swap is noticeable. Revathi has a tiny dark mole near the inner end of her left brow. It is dark and off-centre, not a red bindi, but worth watching. Otherwise on beat: Nagoji (clean chin, curled moustache, flush stud, topknot, grey temples) looks up at the beams. Revathi is propped on her right elbow, holding the cloth up with her left hand, and has her jasmine, coin necklace, armlets and sandalwood line. Hands are sound and there is no painted text. Balloons fit over the beams and paddy bundles at the top, or the white cloth at the bottom.

Minor: her necklace reads as round beads more than flat coins, and a little night sky shows through the storeroom beyond the door, which reads as a far doorway out to the courtyard. Otherwise clean: Revathi, dressed, at the top of the steps with one hand on the open door and looking back down. There is blue moonlight on the clay vessels beyond and the guttering brass lamp with smoke in the foreground. The upper-left earth wall is clear for her long balloon.

Minor: the foreground lamp is a wide brass bowl with a central spout, not the small stand lamp seen in 13.2 and 13.3. It still reads as a brass oil lamp with its wick gone dark and one thread of smoke rising. Only one foot is visible, the other hidden behind it, which is plausible. Otherwise clean. The shut door at the top of the steps has a hairline of moonlight at its edges, and the cellar is near-dark with jars and paddy bundles. Nagoji lies on the mat with eyes open looking up: topknot, grey temples, curled moustache, clean chin, flush gold stud, and the ridged brand and scar on his raised left forearm. No painted text. Three captions fit on the dark wall above him between the pillar and the jars, and in the upper right under the beams, clear of the smoke and his eyes.
